niche.habitat: Hyphal overburden & karst exhalation zones where network source-sink dynamics concentrate resources
niche.diet: Chemoautotrophic symbiont; digests fungal exudates, ion gradients, and spore dust via external enzymatic hydrolysis. 'Wants' network stability and spore dispersal over personal reproduction.
niche.active: Nocturnal and crepuscular; activity pulses match chemical diffusion cycles (hours to days)

body: Ribbon-like, segmented chitin-glucan carapace with melanin streaks; ventral ciliated chemosensory pits; slow cytoplasmic circulation. Evolved as a biological modem to interface with the network’s slow chemical and contested electrical signalling.

skill.effect: Reveals hidden resource paths within an 8m radius

chains.weakness: Sudden VOC bursts blind receptors for 2 turns

journal.en: It doesn't hunt; it listens to the soil breathe.

journal.en: Time moves differently here, and so does it.

plausibility.summary: Bradykinetic creeping on the order of metres per hour fits oligotrophic external-digestion foraging (F13, F16) and tracking slow resource fronts (F14, F19). Hyphal overburden and karst exhalation moisture support traction; rapid desiccation on bare carbonate (F10, F17) is a credible trade-off at 15 m visibility and patchy humidity.

relations.note: (council kind 'commensal') Siltfilter grazes on the same benthic detritus, inadvertently clearing hyphal paths; Sustrisoma rides the siltfilter’s gill rakers to reach higher nutrient fronts.

body_plan.origin: descended from benthic detritivores that colonized hyphal overburden

temperament: Patient, resource-equilibrium seeking, easily startled by sudden pH or voltage shifts. Behaves less like an individual and more like a distributed node in the mycelial ‘mind’.
secrets: If the player administers a precise electrical micro-pulse, the creature will temporarily broadcast the network’s resource map, but the feedback delay can cause stamina rot if not timed with the creature’s bradykinetic rhythm.
Its melanin patterns encode historical carbon flows; reading them backwards reveals where the network previously starved.
It avoids places where the player’s enzyme patches were too acidic, leaving behind crystalline salt rings that mark safe zones.
moments: When the first rain falls, its melanin bands pulse in perfect unison with the fungal network, and for a moment it feels less like an animal and more like the forest’s own slow heartbeat.

journal.en: It doesn't think; it remembers the soil.
To talk to the network, you must first learn to wait.
